events.title: Dionysius is elected bishop of Rome after Valerian's persecution
events.description: Dionysius was elected bishop of Rome almost a year after Pope Sixtus II was killed in Emperor Valerian's persecution of Christians. His pontificate saw the toleration issued by Gallienus in 260, and he assigned presbyters to individual parishes.

events.title: The Abbasids defeat Emperor Theophilos at the Battle of Anzen
events.description: Forces of the Abbasid Caliphate defeated a Byzantine army led by Emperor Theophilos at Anzen, or Dazimon, near present-day Dazman in Turkey. In the same year the Abbasids sacked Amorion.

events.title: Godfrey of Bouillon is elected to rule Jerusalem
events.description: At a council in the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, after Raymond of Toulouse had refused the crown, Godfrey of Bouillon was elected to rule Jerusalem. He took the title Advocate, or Defender, of the Holy Sepulchre rather than king.

events.title: Crusaders sack Béziers and massacre its people
events.description: The army of the Albigensian Crusade stormed Béziers and killed much of its population. A chronicler later attributed to the papal legate the words 'Kill them all; God will know his own'.

events.title: A north German coalition defeats Valdemar II at Bornhöved
events.description: Near Bornhöved in Holstein, an army of Lübeck, Hamburg, Dithmarschen, Holstein and north German nobles under Count Adolf IV of Schauenburg and Holstein defeated King Valdemar II of Denmark. Valdemar lost most of his German conquests but kept Estonia.

events.title: Edward I defeats William Wallace at Falkirk
events.description: English longbowmen broke the Scottish spear formations at Falkirk, ending Wallace's career as a field commander. He was captured and executed in 1305.

events.title: St. Mary Magdalene's flood strikes central Europe
events.description: The largest recorded flood in central Europe struck on and around the feast day of St. Mary Magdalene, and became known by her name. Its water levels exceeded those of the 2002 European floods, making it the worst such event on record for the region.

events.title: Schwyz and its allies defeat Zürich at St. Jakob an der Sihl
events.description: At the gates of Zürich, the confederate army led by Schwyz defeated the Zürich forces and their Austrian allies; the burgomaster Rudolf Stüssi was killed defending the Sihl bridge. The confederates then besieged Zürich.

events.title: John White's colonists arrive at Roanoke Island
events.description: More than 100 English settlers led by John White landed at Roanoke, intending to found the 'City of Ralegh'. When White returned in 1590 they had vanished, becoming the 'Lost Colony'.

events.title: Hood attacks Sherman in the Battle of Atlanta
events.description: Confederate General John Bell Hood struck Sherman's armies east of Atlanta, killing Union General James McPherson. The attack failed, and Atlanta's fall in September boosted Lincoln's re-election.

events.title: Wiley Post completes the first solo flight around the world
events.description: Wiley Post landed at Floyd Bennett Field, New York, after circling the globe alone in 7 days, 18 hours and 49 minutes. An autopilot and radio direction-finder made the feat possible.

song: Tamil Shaivas, devotees of Shiva in South India
Hymns to the god Shiva by three Tamil poet-saints who lived some 1,300 years ago; they are still sung every day in temples of Tamil Nadu.
